the_normalizing_move.claim: A STEP IS A PROCESS. An artifact is not a step — it is how a step COMPLETES.
the_normalizing_move.why: Akien's list alternates process, artifact, process, artifact. Given the five questions he asked, only the processes can answer them: an artifact has no trigger, consumes nothing, and emits itself. Asking the five questions of an artifact produces a degenerate row that adds nothing — the reify trap.
the_normalizing_move.what_it_collapses: 'what does it emit?' and 'how does it complete?' are the SAME question for every step but two. A step completes when its emitted artifact is through its door. That is Law 4 and Law 8 applied to the pipeline itself: completion is evidence, not assertion.
the_normalizing_move.the_two_exceptions_are_load_bearing: WATCH and LEARN. The probe emits repeatedly, on a clock nobody controls, and completes on RETIREMENT rather than on emission — which is exactly why LEARNME as a boat STATE was wrong: a state parks the boat, and the probe's output is not on the boat's clock. LEARN completes on a DIRECTION, not on an artifact at all. Everywhere else, emit and complete are one question.

learning_is_the_terminal_step.ruled: Akien, 2026-08-04, reading v1 of this note: 'we just removed learning but now that i can see the chart, learning is the terminal state. once feedback is headed in the right direction.' v1 said learning was not a step. v1 was wrong.
learning_is_the_terminal_step.why_the_completion_predicate_is_the_inte: 'Once feedback is headed in the RIGHT DIRECTION' is not 'the feedback arrived' and not 'the thing is correct'. It is a DERIVATIVE — a trend, not a value. That is Law 9's building site stated as a completion predicate: green accretes, and the terminal condition is trending-correctly rather than done. Every other step in this catalog completes on a thing existing; this one completes on a slope. It is the only completion predicate in the system that cannot be satisfied by a single artifact.
learning_is_the_terminal_step.cc_reading_marked_as_cc_reading_and_open: This does NOT resurrect LEARNME as a workflow state on the boat. Akien's standing ruling stands untouched: WATCHME completes when the probe is CREATED, and the boat is done there. LEARN is a step in the CATALOG that no boat ever sits in — which is the sharpest evidence yet that the catalog is not the state machine but a superset of it. If that reading is wrong and the boat does get a terminal state back, it is one word from him and this paragraph dies.
learning_is_the_terminal_step.what_it_exposed_and_akien_immediately_cl: v2 said LEARN needs a JUDGE that does not exist. Akien, same day: 'generally the thing it feeds back into needs to be either one of the design/ticket steps, or to whichever learning block it belongs to. there are a few exceptions, like if you put a probe somewhere to validate that some is or is not doing something, but mostly, it's back to the extant learning loop. it's one of the inputs.' NO JUDGE IS NEEDED AND NONE SHOULD BE BUILT. Feedback is an ORDINARY INPUT to a loop that already exists — not privileged mail, not a verdict, not a new component. This is Law 1 catching me mid-invention.
the_three_destinations_all_extant: the learning block / nexus the probe belongs to — the DEFAULT. Feedback arrives as one input among the nexus's others (code floor, tree, ceiling). Candidate landing, unconfirmed: it becomes a NODE in that nexus's tree, which is [[librarian-graph-tree-thread]]'s existing mechanism rather than a new one.
design or ticket — when the feedback says the intention itself was wrong. Re-entry, not a new door.

a ticket directly — the exception Akien named (a probe placed to validate that something is or is not doing a thing). Already has a name in the corpus: the trouble-ticket shape from his ticket/probe/task tree, 'a kind of probe whose output becomes a ticket'. Prior art, not a new class.
learning_is_the_terminal_step.so_the_address_is_stamped_at_birth_not_l: The probe is created at WATCHME by a node that knows exactly what it is and which loop it came from. So the return address is a FIELD ON THE PROBE, stamped at creation. Feedback does not need to be routed; it is already addressed. That is the whole of [[held-feedback-loops-have-addresses]] — the address is provenance.
learning_is_the_terminal_step.and_it_makes_the_completion_rule_consist: CC READING, marked as mine: LEARN completes on DELIVERY to that address — the same shape as WATCHME completing on probe CREATION. Neither step waits on the world. 'Headed in the right direction' is then the RECEIVING LOOP's standing condition, which is the only place it can honestly live, because a loop is the only thing that can see a trend. Two steps at the docked end, both completing on handoff, one rule rather than two exceptions.
learning_is_the_terminal_step.the_red_shrank_from_a_component_to_a_fie: v2 called learn 'the sharpest unowned thing in the system — no skill, no door, no owner, no judge, no address'. Four of those five were my invention. The real remainder: the probe has no return-address field, and no loop has an inbox. That is small, buildable, and rides work already open.

the_step_schema.name: the step's stable handle. The ticketer SELECTS BY THIS, so it is an id, not a label.
the_step_schema.trigger: what FIRES it — an event, never a clock — AND the skill that carries it, named. A trigger with no skill beside it is a step Akien has to remember to start.
the_step_schema.consumes: the TYPED artifact it takes in. Must equal the previous step's `emits` or the seam is a gap.
the_step_schema.completes: the predicate that makes it done, AND the skill/door that decides it. For most steps: 'the emitted artifact passed its door'.
the_step_schema.gate: the door, and WHAT IT REQUIRES — compiled from the door itself, never transcribed. Absent contract is not an empty one: a door with no requirements passes everything.
the_step_schema.owner: NEW in v2, and it was missing. Law 6: the emitted artifact has exactly one owner, and the door IS that owner's gate. A step whose artifact has no owner has no gate that can mean anything.
the_step_schema.exits: NEW in v2. Steps do not only complete forward. /intent has TWO exits (routed_forward, routed_out) and the kill is the cheaper and more valuable one (Law 1). A catalog that records only forward completion cannot express a kill, and cannot express a workflow with a branch.
the_step_schema.kind: joint (Akien + CC) | mine (CC alone) | device (a component, unattended). A DIAL, not a taxonomy — the cocoon aim is rows migrating rightward. It is also the cost column: 'joint' is the only kind that spends Akien. See [[cocoon-settle-stages-around-cc]].

the_steps.name: capture
the_steps.trigger: Akien has an idea and says so. ENTRY POINT — the only step whose input is outside the system (the picture in his head). Nothing upstream can fire it.
the_steps.completes: the file exists in the ideas queue
the_steps.gate: NONE — no door, and no CairnCommons/ideas/ folder either
the_steps.owner: unowned — nothing gates writes to the ideas queue because there is no queue
the_steps.red: wholly — this lot has not been broken ground on

the_steps.name: intend
the_steps.trigger: reaching for an idea IS the event; no separate trigger is needed. Ideas sit in a queue; /intent's door is the filter.
the_steps.emits: a berth (node in intention fill-state, traced, challenged) AND the source idea marked transformed
the_steps.completes: the berth path is printed by the door
the_steps.gate_requires: 8 fields, compiled live from skills/intent/intention+why.json input_contract: what, how, traces_to, shape, falsifier, challenge, exit, bullets. Refusal names EVERY lack in one pass and is itself recorded.
exits: routed_out — the kill, forced to carry bullets and a challenge pass
the_steps.red: the back-reference. /intent consumes CONVERSATION, not an idea file, and nothing marks the idea transformed. Akien wrote that half explicitly; it does not exist.

the_steps.name: design
the_steps.trigger: a berth exists in intention fill-state and is not yet cast — a PREDICATE ON A BERTH, therefore something a shim could fire on, not a thing Akien has to remember.
the_steps.trigger_skill: NONE — and see open_and_deliberately_unanswered; this may be correct rather than missing
the_steps.emits: cast tickets (typed, gates bound, watch answered)
the_steps.gate_requires: 12 fields, compiled live from skills/sorted/intention+why.json — the largest contract in the system, including assumption_check (the completeness question answered in substance; a one-word pass is the hollow check the door exists to stop) and bullets forced at BOTH exits.
exits: spawns children — the branch the linear drawing hides
the_steps.red: the longest step in the chain, entered by conversation with no shape. /challenge fires at its start (at birth); /sorted closes it; the middle is unnamed.

the_steps.name: chart
the_steps.trigger: a cast ticket is about to become a build. /sail refuses without a chart chain, so the refusal downstream IS the trigger.
the_steps.consumes: cast ticket — BUT see the seam check: chart's input is typed as 'a request', not as a ticket
the_steps.emits: build packet (seven nexus stages, per-field provenance)
the_steps.completes: all seven stages through their schema gates
the_steps.gate: SEVEN doors — BUILT, refuse complete-in-one-pass, accumulate-then-raise
the_steps.gate_requires: NOT COMPILABLE TODAY. The seven gates are schemas in cairn/chart/*.py; the skill's charter declares NO input_contract, so `skill_block contract chart` prints a refusal, not a list. Two gate mechanisms, one of them invisible to the catalog. Measured 2026-08-04.
exits: stage refusal — back to the same stage
the_steps.red: the gate is real but unreadable by anything but a human opening the source. The most complete step in the chain is also the one the catalog can see least of.

the_steps.name: build
the_steps.completes: code exists — NOT that it is right
the_steps.gate: /sail refuses on a missing chart chain — BUILT
the_steps.gate_requires: NOT DECLARED. skills/sail/intention+why.json has no input_contract; the door's real requirement (a chart chain, an intent_berth on the ticket) lives only in code and prose.
the_steps.owner: the component being built (Law 6: its own directory)
the_steps.note: 'Proposed' is doing real work in Akien's word choice: this step's completion predicate is deliberately weak, because the next step is what makes it true. Law 9 lives in that word.

the_steps.name: test
the_steps.trigger_skill: none needed — the tester is a device
the_steps.completes: the seal is written through the validation door
exits: red seal — and a red seal is a completion, not a failure of the step
the_steps.kind: DEVICE — the only fully-device step in the chain today
the_steps.red: live trouble: the door is not the only path to the file. A hand-write destroys a proof's seal history silently and looks exactly like a fresh seal.

the_steps.name: watchme
the_steps.emits: a probe — addressed to wherever feedback has to come from (gateway, time, future event)
the_steps.completes: THE PROBE IS CREATED. Akien's standing ruling; the state does not wait for what the probe finds.

the_steps.name: watch
the_steps.trigger: whatever the probe was addressed to
exits: emits and continues — the only step that completes without stopping emitting
the_steps.red: wholly — but BaseShim already carries the three memories this needs (_was_true anti-bounce, _cleared terminal/retired, _first_seen feeding overdue()). The retirement predicate is _cleared. Prior art in-house, not a fresh design.

the_steps.name: learn
the_steps.added: v2, 2026-08-04, Akien: 'learning is the terminal state. once feedback is headed in the right direction.'
the_steps.trigger_skill: NONE — /moreabout is the invocable learning signal but it is a PULL, and this is a PUSH arriving unbidden
the_steps.completes: DELIVERY to the probe's return address (CC reading). 'Headed in the right direction' is the receiving loop's standing condition, not a gate learn must pass — a loop is the only thing that can see a trend.
the_steps.completes_skill: NONE built — but no judge is needed. The receiver is an extant loop.
the_steps.owner: DERIVED, per probe: the learning block / nexus the probe belongs to, or the design/ticket step it re-enters. Not a fixed owner — a stamped one.
exits: delivered to its nexus — the default
re-enters at design or ticket when the intention itself was wrong
becomes a ticket directly — the validation-probe exception, the trouble-ticket shape
the_steps.kind: device once the address is a field — the delivery is mechanical. Only the loop's own judgement is joint.
the_steps.red: TWO THINGS, both small: the probe carries no return-address field, and no loop has an inbox. Everything else about this step already exists.

the_empty_cell_is_the_red_lot.claim: This catalog is the SITE PLAN that green-is-earned-not-assumed has been held at THINKME waiting for, and the mechanism it was waiting on just arrived.
the_empty_cell_is_the_red_lot.why: That ticket is held because the naive mechanism — a field on every component saying red or green — reproduces the defect exactly: a hand-set field is one more thing that can be wrong, and nothing checks it. Its why_beneath_the_why says the artifact wanted is 'closer to a SITE PLAN than to a health check — it must be able to show the lots nobody has broken ground on yet, which no test-result-derived signal can see.' A step catalog with a gate column does exactly that. Nobody marks capture red. Capture is red because its gate cell is EMPTY and nothing can fill it.
the_empty_cell_is_the_red_lot.measured_2026_08_04: 3 of 9 skills declare an input_contract (intent 8 fields, sorted 12, saveslate 7). Six declare none — challenge, chart, commit, moreabout, note, sail — and for those the compiler prints a refusal that names the lack in its own words: 'An absent contract is NOT an empty one: a door with no requirements passes everything, which is the vacuous gate this build exists to avoid.' The red is not asserted by a reader. It is the compiler declining to fill a cell.
the_empty_cell_is_the_red_lot.so_the_rule: The catalog must be COMPILED, never hand-maintained. A hand-written gate column is stale the moment a charter changes, and a stale site plan is worse than none. Prior art for the whole shape: intentions-congruency-lab/ (compiled folder, one file per source) and recompile_gate.sh (the READ is the event that refreshes; no daemon watches on anyone's behalf).

what_normalizing_revealed.1_the_workflow_states_are_a_projection_o: THINKME~design, TICKETME~casting, BUILDME~chart+build, PROVEME~test, PROVED~validation sealed, WATCHME~watchme. The pipeline is the SYSTEM's view; the stage is ONE NODE's view of the same seams. This is why 'a workflow is composed at ticketing time by the ticketer' — the workflow is a per-instance SELECTION from this catalog, which Akien confirmed 2026-08-04 ('EXACTLY right').
what_normalizing_revealed.2_the_catalog_is_a_superset_of_the_state: learn is a step no boat sits in — the boat retired at WATCHME. So the catalog cannot be derived from the workflow states, and the workflow states cannot be derived from the catalog. They are two projections of the same seams, and only the catalog can hold a step with no boat in it.
what_normalizing_revealed.3_the_two_ends_have_no_physics_and_that_: The states cover the MIDDLE only. Before THINKME the boat does not exist; after WATCHME it has docked. Those ends are exactly the four steps with no door (capture, watchme, watch, learn) and exactly the ends we independently knew were missing. The gap in the physics and the gap in the pipeline are one gap.
what_normalizing_revealed.4_the_trigger_column_is_the_footprint_di: Triggers that are 'Akien types a command': 5 of 9. The founding intention is getting him out of running the system; this column makes the distance COUNTABLE instead of felt. Kin [[shrinking-footprint-event-not-poll]].
what_normalizing_revealed.5_the_kind_column_is_the_cocoon_dial_and: 1 device, 2 nominally-device-but-unbuilt, 2 mine, 3 joint, 1 undecided. 'Joint' is the only kind that spends Akien, so the same column that measures the cocoon measures the cost of composing a workflow out of these steps.
what_normalizing_revealed.6_the_skill_column_is_the_gap_akien_was_: He asked for the skill to show in trigger and completes, and said 'that's part of the gap i was looking for'. Counted: 4 of 9 steps have a skill at their trigger, 5 of 9 have one at their completion. Every blank is a step a human has to start or stop by hand. It renders the same fact as the footprint dial but at the place a reader can act on it.
what_normalizing_revealed.7_type_matching_across_seams_is_a_mechan: If step N's emits ≠ step N+1's consumes, the seam is a gap. capture emits 'idea record', intend consumes CONVERSATION (gap — Akien's own '?'). design emits 'cast tickets', chart consumes 'a request' (gap — chart's input is not typed as a ticket). chart→build→test→watchme→watch→learn all match. Two gaps, both found by the check rather than by reading.
what_normalizing_revealed.8_the_gate_column_has_two_mechanisms_and: skill_block contracts live in charters and compile. chart's seven gates live in code and do not. So the most gated step in the system is the one the catalog can see least of — which is exactly backwards, and is a finding the gate column produced on its first run.

what_this_is_for.akien: 'so i can be reminded and so we can communicate it with others' — the catalog is a SHOWABLE surface, not a note. Two renders from one compiled source: a text render for the terminal, and a PANE on the one web server (never a new route, never a new server — [[one-web-server-surfaces-in-the-shim]]).
what_this_is_for.eventually: 'we'll have such a list for all workflows all their parts.' This pipeline is workflow #1. The catalog is the class-level artifact; a workflow is a selection from it; a boat's cursor is a position in that selection. Three things we have been treating separately are one thing seen from three distances.

the_challenge_pass.better_approach: Skip the catalog, fix the marked gaps directly. Rejected: the schema found gaps nobody marked (chart's untyped input; chart's invisible gate; learn's missing judge; the missing owner column) and turned two prose dials into counts. But do NOT build enforcement from it yet — see hidden_assumption.
the_challenge_pass.prior_art: In-house: workflow state strings, the /chart nexus stages, BaseShim's three memories, intentions-congruency-lab (compiled folder), recompile_gate.sh (read-is-the-event), [[held-workflow-belongs-to-the-author]], [[held-feedback-loops-have-addresses]]. External, cited not grafted: superpowers types Consumes/Produces per task for the same reason — so a step's neighbours are typed. Idea borrowed, no bytes.
the_challenge_pass.hidden_assumption: That the pipeline is LINEAR. It is not: /intent routes OUT, /sorted spawns children, a bug enters directly at TICKET, learn re-enters at capture. v2 adds the `exits` field so the catalog can HOLD that instead of hiding it — but the drawing is still a spine, and anything built from it must handle branch and exit or it will refuse legitimate shapes.
the_challenge_pass.real_collision: 'step' vs 'stage' vs 'stratum' — not a collision (a stage is a step seen from one node) but close enough to drift. Akien used 'step' first here, so step is the pipeline's unit and stage stays the node's. Flagged out loud. Kin [[terms-drift-flag-coinages]].
the_challenge_pass.back_up: PROCEED, still as a held note. Do not cast, do not enforce. The one thing with a real ticket behind it is the compiled render, because green-is-earned-not-assumed is already open and this is its mechanism.

open_and_deliberately_unanswered: Whether 'design' should have a skill at all, or whether it is correctly the one step that stays conversational — the place where the picture in Akien's head enters, which by [[spec-lives-in-akiens-head]] is the one thing no device can take over. If true, design is not a gap; it is the irreducible joint step, and the honest catalog should say so rather than leave a blank cell that reads as unbuilt. Note this now cuts both ways: learn's judge may be the same irreducible thing.
